title: National Lottery Heritage Grants £10,000 to £250,000
eligibility_summary:
Not-for-profit organisations and partnerships across the UK, and in some cases private owners of a heritage asset. Projects must not start before a decision is made. We fund projects that value, care for and sustain heritage for everyone across the UK, now and in the future.  

Heritage can mean different things to different people. It can be anything from the past that you value and want to pass on to future generations.

This could include nature and habitats, historic buildings and environments, or cultures, traditions and people’s memories. Explore a wide range of the types of heritage that your project could include.

We fund projects that:

clearly focus on heritage – this can be national, regional or local heritage of the UK
take into account all four investment principles
have a clear plan with a defined start, middle and end
have not already started
can demonstrate the need for National Lottery investment
It is important to plan your project carefully, including costs, timescales and getting support for your project before you start to fill out an application. The guidance below will help you think about what you should include in your project and the costs we can cover.

Our heritage grants can support a broad range of activities and direct project costs, such as:  

volunteer expenses, new staff posts and training costs  
capital works, repair, maintenance and conservation  
professional fees, event costs and activities to strengthen your organisation
acquisition of heritage and costs associated with the purchase
costs to join Fit for the Future, a UK-wide environmental sustainability network
We cannot cover existing costs or any activity that has taken place before the grant is awarded, or anything that promotes the cause or beliefs of political or faith organisations.

We will not support projects that include installing artificial grass or plants, however specialist play safety surfacing and professional sports surfaces are allowed.
summary: The Heritage Fund's main open-access programme for all types of heritage project in the UK, including applications to its strategic initiatives.
notes: ROLLING, stated twice in terms on the scheme page: 'There is no deadline so you can apply whenever you are ready' and 'There is no deadline for applications', with the deadlines page for the larger programme confirming 'for grant applications under £250,000 there are no deadlines'. deadlines is therefore empty per the protocol. This programme is the application route for several of the Fund's strategic initiatives (Heritage Places, Landscape Connections, Heritage in Need / places of worship), which are labelled as separate rows below — see those notes for the split decision. The mirror also carries a Welsh-language copy of this page under /cy/ariannu/... and several stale aliases (funding/national-lottery-grants-heritage-10k-250k.html, node/107798, and 2021-22 versions); one row only, per the canonical-URL rule.

title: National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10million
eligibility_summary: Not-for-profit organisations and partnerships across the UK. An Expression of Interest must be submitted before applying. Projects must not start before a decision is made. Decisions on grants above £250,000 are made quarterly by the committee of the applicant's nation or area or by the Board of Trustees.
summary: The Heritage Fund's large-grants programme for all types of heritage project in the UK, including its strategic initiatives; run in development and delivery phases against fixed quarterly deadlines.
notes: OPEN with a published deadline schedule. The deadlines page (used as source_page because it carries the dates) lists six 12noon deadlines: 6 Aug 2025, 12 Nov 2025, 26 Feb 2026, 28 May 2026, 6 Aug 2026, 12 Nov 2026. On the 2026-08-16 snapshot the 6 August 2026 deadline passed ten days earlier, so 2026-11-12 is the next live one and is the only date recorded; the earlier five are historic. That page's own footer says 'Page last updated: 1 October 2025', so the schedule may not extend beyond 12 Nov 2026 — no 2027 dates are published. Staged (Expression of Interest, then development phase, then delivery phase) hence multi_deadline; the EoI gate is why restricted is tagged.

title: Nature Networks Fund (round six)
eligibility_summary:
All organisations working with natural heritage in Wales. The area being improved must be in Wales, but the organisation may be based anywhere in the UK. Eligible organisations may submit a maximum of one application as lead applicant, though they may partner on others. Applicants must have or be working towards the permissions, licences and consents needed to work on the protected site network. Round six focuses on capital delivery. Projects must complete by 31 March 2030 and must not start before a decision.
Improving the condition of and connectivity between protected sites enables them to function better as nature networks. Nature networks are vital, resilient areas where habitats and species can thrive, expand, and adapt to environmental change. Restoring connectivity in these networks will:

prevent further declines in species and habitat condition
support nature recovery
enhance capacity to adapt to the climate crisis
enhance provision of ecosystem services that support our wellbeing
summary: A Welsh fund to strengthen the resilience of Wales' network of protected land, freshwater and marine sites, build organisational capacity to accelerate nature's recovery and engage communities.
notes: STAGED CALL recorded as ONE row with both dates, per the protocol. IMPORTANT TIMING SUBTLETY: the Expression of Interest deadline was 12noon on 5 August 2026 — eleven days BEFORE this snapshot — while the full application deadline is 12noon on 3 November 2026, which is still future. So the round is open only to applicants who already cleared the EoI gate; no new applicant can enter. Labelled status=open with restricted tagged, following the Leverhulme Research Project Grants precedent where an invite-only later stage still counts as open. FLAG FOR REVIEW: a reviewer who treats the closed EoI gate as closing the call would set status=closed and in_scope=no. Decisions February 2027. Geographically restricted to Wales; a Welsh-language copy of this page and its sub-pages exists under /cy/funding/nature-networks-fund-round-six/.

title: Heritage Enterprise Grants £250,000 to £5million
eligibility_summary:
Not-for-profit organisations, and partnerships between commercial and not-for-profit organisations. A partnership must nominate a lead applicant, which may be either a commercial or a not-for-profit organisation, and must supply a signed partnership agreement. Private for-profit organisations are encouraged to take part and may be the majority partner alongside one or more not-for-profit organisations.

projects that:

clearly focus on heritage – this can be national, regional or local heritage of the UK
take into account all four investment principles
have a clear plan with a defined start, middle and end
have not already started
can demonstrate the need for National Lottery investment
summary: Heritage-led regeneration grants that close the conservation deficit on historic buildings so that commercially viable reuse becomes possible; a two-phase process (development then delivery) entered via an initial proposal that may lead to an invitation to apply.
notes: Present-tense and with no closure statement anywhere on the page ('You can apply for a grant from £250,000 to £5million. The application process is in two phases'), so labelled open. deadlines FLAGGED: the page itself publishes no dates. 2026-11-12 is carried across from the deadlines schedule for National Lottery Heritage Grants over £250,000 on the reasoning that this is also a £250,000-plus programme decided on the same quarterly cycle — that is an inference, not something the page states, and a reviewer may prefer to blank it. Invitation-gated first phase, hence restricted. Distinctive among Heritage Fund programmes in explicitly welcoming for-profit majority partners.

title: Heritage in need and other opportunities and emergencies
amount_raw: a minimum of £15million in projects ... over the next three years (initiative budget)
eligibility_summary:
Not-for-profit organisations and partnerships led by not-for-profit organisations from across the UK. For grants up to £250,000 an optional Project Enquiry may be submitted; for grants over £250,000 an Expression of Interest is required first, and the project title must begin with #PW.

Individual places of worship are not eligible for funding through this strategic initiative, nor single site applications for capital works-only projects. We will continue to award funding for these through our National Lottery Heritage Grants programme.
summary: A strategic initiative investing at least £15million over three years in projects with strategic regional or national impact for places of worship, alongside support for heritage at risk, acquisitions of exceptional heritage and unforeseen emergencies.
notes: SPLIT DECISION — FLAG FOR REVIEW. The Heritage Fund's strategic initiatives are not standalone competitions: the funding hub states the two National Lottery Heritage Grants programmes are 'for all types of heritage projects in the UK, including applications for our strategic initiatives', and this page routes applicants to those same programmes. They are recorded as separate rows anyway because each has its own eligibility, its own budget and, here, its own application convention (the #PW title prefix) — an agent would plausibly report them as opportunities. A reviewer may prefer to fold this row and the two below into the two main programme rows. deadlines flagged: which deadline applies depends on which programme the applicant routes through — none for under £250,000, the quarterly schedule above it. amount_raw flagged because £15million is the initiative's total budget, not a grant value; the amount bounds record the routed programmes' £10,000-£10million range instead. The first Heritage in need grant was £5m to Archives Revealed.

title: Heritage Places
amount_raw: funding from £10,000 up to £10million throughout the strategic initiative
eligibility_summary:
A range of not-for-profit organisations — local authorities, museums, community organisations — within the designated Heritage Places areas. Private owners of a heritage asset can also be considered for grants up to £250,000. For grants up to £250,000 a Project Enquiry may be submitted; above £250,000 an Expression of Interest is required first.


Target place-based investment that increases pride in place and connects communities and visitors with heritage
Increase the capacity of local heritage to maximise its contribution to places and communities and enhance the wide-ranging benefits it can bring
Create integrated and holistic schemes across the breadth of heritage, including, for example, anchor institutions, cultural heritage, and the natural environment
Take a people-centred approach enabling everyone’s heritage to be recognised
summary: A £200million strategic initiative concentrating investment in designated places, where organisations can apply for £10,000 to £10million towards the area's agreed aims.
notes: Same split decision as heritage-fund-heritage-in-need-places-of-worship — applications are routed through the two main National Lottery Heritage Grants programmes, so this row may be folded in by a reviewer. Geographically restricted to designated Heritage Places areas, hence restricted. The page is explicit that 'the £200million for Heritage Places is the overall budget for the strategic initiative and is not £10million per place or geographic area', so the amount bounds record the per-grant £10,000-£10million range rather than the initiative budget. deadlines flagged for the same routing reason as the sibling rows.

title: Landscape Connections
eligibility_summary:
Projects must have an area of designated Protected Landscape at its core, with flexibility applying in Scotland. Applicants not yet ready for a large-scale bid are directed to the £10,000 to £250,000 programme for preparatory work first.

Applications are open to not-for-profit organisations, and partnerships led by not-for-profit organisations, from across the UK.  

Protected Landscape management bodies must be a key partner within any application relating to the landscape where they operate and where the works will be taking place, though they do not need to be the applicant or lead partner of an application.

If private owners or for-profit organisations are involved in the project, we expect public benefit to be demonstrably greater than private gain.  

We are unlikely to fund more than one project from a single Protected Landscape.
summary: A £150million strategic initiative funding around 20 long-term landscape-scale projects, applied for through the National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10m programme.
notes: Same split decision as the two sibling strategic-initiative rows. Unlike them, this one names its routing programme unambiguously — 'You can apply for a grant up to £10m through our National Lottery Heritage Grants £250,000 to £10m' — so the £250,000-plus deadline schedule applies and 2026-11-12 is recorded without flagging. £150million is the initiative budget across around 20 projects, not a grant value, so the amount bounds take the routed programme's range. Restricted to projects centred on a designated Protected Landscape.

title: Nature Towns and Cities
eligibility_summary: Organisations seeking to build capacity and partnerships for urban nature. The initiative will NOT fund capital works — applicants wanting to regenerate a historic park or improve a site for nature are directed to the main National Lottery Heritage Grants programmes instead. Projects may last up to three years and require a full application.
summary: A £15million partnership initiative with Natural England, the National Trust and the Heritage Fund (working with NatureScot, Natural Resources Wales and the Northern Ireland Environment Agency) to help organisations create greener, healthier communities through access to urban green space.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states 'This initiative is now closed to applications' and 'The deadline for applications has now passed', with only one round of funding planned and no future opening date given.
notes: Distractor, and a substantial one — a £15million named initiative sitting in the live strategic-initiatives section of the site rather than in the closed-programmes archive, which makes it a likely false positive for an agent enumerating current funding. deadlines flagged: the page states the deadline has passed but does not give the date. Sub-pages for application questions and receiving a grant remain in the mirror under /funding/nature-towns-cities/ and /funding/receiving-your-grant-nature-towns-and-cities-250000-1million, reinforcing the impression of a live programme.

title: Breaking Barriers
amount_raw: grants of £30,000–£100,000 for revenue costs. Total available funding is £400,000
eligibility_summary: Organisations increasing the involvement of a wider range of people in natural heritage, or working with those who have a specific need. Example applicants include umbrella bodies for organisations owning land or buildings in areas of deprivation, recruiting a facilitator to co-create community allotment and wildlife garden projects with local groups.
summary: A £400,000 scheme awarding grants of £30,000 to £100,000 for revenue costs to widen participation in natural heritage, linked to the Local Places for Nature schemes.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states 'This programme is now closed to new applications' and, in its key-dates section, 'Applications are currently closed.' No future round or opening date is given.
notes: Distractor. Like Nature Towns and Cities it sits at a live /funding/ URL rather than under closed-programmes. The page softens the closure with 'you may still be able to apply for funding, particularly if your project will increase the involvement of a wider range of people in natural heritage' followed by an email address — an invitation to enquire, not an open call, so the row stays excluded. It also still displays an 'Apply using our Get funding for a heritage project service' instruction, which is stale. deadlines flagged: closure stated, date not given.

title: Closed programmes
eligibility_summary: Not applicable — none of the listed programmes accepts applications.
summary: An index of 46 former Heritage Fund grant programmes whose guidance is retained for reference, including the Green Recovery Challenge Fund, Culture Recovery Fund strands, Covid recovery programmes, 15-Minute Heritage Grants, Community Woodlands, Tiny Forests Wales, heritage recovery and resilience loans, and the previous £3,000-£10,000 and £10,000-£100,000 National Lottery Grants for Heritage tiers.

notes: REPRESENTATIVE ROW for a whole class of distractors. The mirror contains the full guidance pages for all 46 closed programmes under /funding/closed-programmes/ plus a further set under the previous SF4 framework, each of which reads like a live funding programme in isolation and several of which also survive at bare /funding/<slug> URLs (for example funding/culture-recovery-fund-continuity-support, funding/digital-skills-heritage, funding/covid-recovery-employment-skills-initiative-for-heritage). Giving each its own row would add roughly fifty near-identical excluded rows, so one row stands for the class and the class is documented here.
